body:
## Summary

The most wrong thing in Formal AI today: **the links network is not the substrate that reasons.** `VISION.md` says "the associative network is the AI". In the running binary the solver reasons over Rust structs (`MemoryStore { events: Vec<MemoryEvent> }`, `EventLog`, `seed::lexicon()`), and the doublets store is a write-behind projection filled after each `.lino` write. Behaviour is 178k lines of Rust, 43 handler files, and hundreds of literal string predicates. Every new capability lands as a Rust handler, a `.lino` recipe that describes the Rust, and a test that pins the two together. The recipes are documentation of code, not executable knowledge.

That inversion sets the self-coding target at "a deterministic symbolic engine edits a 178k-line Rust codebase". Measured against that target, here is exactly how far we are: Formal AI, driven through the Agent CLI, can apply a single-file Rust edit when the prompt names the file and the exact change (32 such leaves pass in the current ladder). It has never chosen an edit from a requirement, never compiled or tested one, and never had one merged. No pull request has ever been opened by a formal-ai model run. Upstream coding benchmarks are 0/20 in every scheduled run for seven weeks. Meanwhile the self-hosting metric credits Claude sessions to Formal AI, the shrink-only handler ceilings were raised twice, and most engineering effort goes into gates and evidence about the system rather than the system.

This issue asks for: (D1) make the links network executable and the Rust a shrinking kernel; (D2) build the missing links-to-code edit path and redefine self-coding to start with links; (D3) make the self-development metric measure the model and the behaviour it changed; (D4) turn the ladder into a compile-and-test coding ladder; (D5 to D9) act on upstream zeros, work the real user frontier, and cut evidence and gate weight. The associative stack (doublets, Links Notation, meta-language, deterministic symbolic reasoning, no neural steering) is the constraint every item is designed inside. The architecture is flexible; everything else may move.

## 1. Verified evidence

All numbers are from `main` at `dda02efb4` (2026-09-07). Each row names the command that reproduces it. Section 8 lists what changed after an adversarial re-check of the first draft.

### 1.1 The reasoning substrate is Rust; the doublets store is a projection

| Measurement | Value | Reproduce |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rust lines / files under `src/` | 178,153 / 509 (only 1 inline `#[test]`, so not test-inflated) | `find src -name '*.rs' \| xargs wc -l \| tail -1` |
| `LinkStore` references in `solver.rs`, `engine.rs`, `main.rs`, `seed.rs` | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 | `grep -c LinkStore src/solver.rs src/engine.rs src/main.rs src/seed.rs` |
| Only runtime construction of the doublets store | `memory_sync.rs:422`, inside `synchronize_link_cli_projection`, called after the `.lino` file is written | `grep -rn 'LinkCliLinkStore::open_at' src` |
| What the solver reads | `MemoryStore` is `Vec<MemoryEvent>` (`memory.rs:126`); `solver.rs` references `MemoryStore`/`EventLog` 5 times and `LinkStore` 0 times | `grep -c 'MemoryStore\|EventLog' src/solver.rs` |
| Handler source files under `src/solver_handlers` | 43 (excluding `mod.rs`, `modules.rs`) | `find src/solver_handlers -name '*.rs' ! -name mod.rs ! -name modules.rs \| wc -l` |
| Literal `contains("` / `starts_with("` in `src/` | 401 / 169 (136 of the `contains` in handlers; top file `shell_command_transform.rs` with 33) | `grep -rc 'contains("' --include='*.rs' src \| sort -t: -k2 -rn` |
| Generated allowlist of user-facing prose literals still in `src/` | 1,309 rows | `scripts/hardcoded-language-allowlist.txt` |
| Handler-migration ledger | 4 migrated, 51 pending | `grep -c 'status pending' data/meta/handler-migration-ledger.lino` |
| The "shrink-only" ceilings | **raised** 37→38 files and 48→49→50 dispatch entries on 2026-08-02 (`d38c6e3cf`) and 2026-08-11 (`1edcf2878`) | `git log -p -- data/meta/handler-migration-ledger.lino` |
| Outside-core lines ceiling (E71) | 19,543 → 19,360 (−0.9 %) since 2026-08-10 | `data/meta/core-boundary-ledger.lino` |
| Rust / seed / tests / docs+logs added in 90 days | +179,693 / +59,710 / +158,908 / **+4,384,789** lines (rename-aware diff gives the same `src` figure) | `git diff --shortstat -M50% 614dfb6a3 HEAD -- src` |

The synthesis behind the curated 13/13 industry suite is illustrative: `synthesize_python_candidate` picks a task by seed role, then branches `if task.slug == "has_close_elements"` and so on, one Rust branch per benchmark task with `&'static str` fragments (`src/solver_handlers/program_synthesis.rs:384-470`). Recognition is data; the solution shape is a Rust branch per task. HumanEval task 0 is `has_close_elements`, and the upstream HumanEval slice still scores 0/20, so the curated pass does not transfer to the upstream prompt format. The case study must explain why.

### 1.2 What Formal AI has actually authored

**Via the ladder.** The current harness (`experiments/issue_1028_agent_cli_ladder/run.sh`, `verify-node.sh`) has 32 change-shaped leaves: 11 list-member insertions ("add `"wikiquote"` to `WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDERS`"), 11 literal replacements, 10 constant renames, each naming the file and the exact text. A leaf passes when the marker is absent before and present after, the anchor survives, exactly one tracked file changed, and `rustfmt` parses it. Nothing runs `cargo check` or `cargo test`; composite nodes verify effect files and never apply both children's diffs to one tree. The last run (2026-08-30, `workflow_dispatch`, `TREE_DEPTH: 5`) passed the 32 leaves; the two pull-request-triggered runs on 2026-08-28 failed. The committed 63/63 evidence in `docs/case-studies/issue-1028/agent-tree-run/` is the older inspect-and-record form of the ladder.

**Via commits.** 125 commits carry a real `Formal-AI-Session` trailer (`git log --format='%(trailers:key=Formal-AI-Session,valueonly)'`). 72 of them (58 %) carry a session id of the form `issue-NNN-claude-2026MMDD`; the sampled evidence file opens with `Agent: formal-ai (Claude Opus 4.8) via /solve` (`dev/log/issues/702/pulls/818/analysis.md:4`). The metric (`scripts/self-hosting-metric.rs::commit_has_formal_ai_evidence`) accepts any commit whose session id appears in a committed file containing the string `formal-ai`, so release `v0.307.0` credits 3,962 of 6,322 changed lines (63 %) to Formal AI on the strength of those Claude sessions. Paths touched by the 125 commits: `docs/case-studies` 417, `data/meta` 165, `dev/log` 76, `tests/unit` 69, `experiments` 79, `data/seed` 28, `.github/workflows` 23, `src/agentic_coding` 20. Of the ten most recent, eight are `docs:` subjects and two are `feat(data)`/`feat(seed)`.

**Via pull requests.** 495 of the 496 pull requests ever opened are under konard's account (`gh pr list --state all --limit 1000 --json author`); 51 of the last 200 merged carry a hosted-agent signature (Hive Mind, Claude Code) in the body. None was opened by a formal-ai model run, and no bot identity or GitHub App exists in `.github/workflows`. The #1021 case study says so directly (`docs/case-studies/issue-1021/README.md:359`), and the three production Hive Mind runs of 2026-08-28 recorded in #1064 all ended in empty pull requests with `planned_not_executed`.

### 1.3 Metrics that report progress without capability

| Metric | What it says | What is true |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Self-hosting share | trailing 1.36 %, target 0.50 % (`data/meta/self-hosting-ledger.lino`, last row); 269,208 of 1,654,028 lines credited since `v0.296.0` | attribution is by trailer, 58 % of attributed sessions are Claude sessions, and the numerator is dominated by case studies and ledgers |
| Release gate (#924, #1066) | one merged session-backed Formal AI PR per cycle, enforced in `release.yml:511-525` | the cheapest satisfier is a documentation commit with trailers; that is what the history shows; the gate held back the #904/#907 fix for 268 commits (#1064) |
| Industry suite | 13/13, cited once in `VISION.md` and three times in `ROADMAP.md`; `README.md` shows neither | upstream `external-results.lino`, 7 scheduled runs 2026-07-20 to 09-07: HumanEval 0/20, MBPP 0/20, GSM8K 2/20, MATH 0/20, object counting 0/20, CoEdIT 0/20, SWE-bench Lite 0/1, all unchanged; only the egg (20/20) and Ascent (5/5) rewrite-engine assertions pass |
| Handler ceilings | shrink-only | raised twice (1.1) |
| E106 (#958), "show the upstream number beside the curated one" | open since 2026-08-04 | no commit references it |

### 1.4 Where the effort goes

| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Commits on `main`, 90 days | 3,671: fix 590, chore 418, docs 413, test 383, **feat 276**, plus 612 merges and 267 "Initial commit with task details" |
| Tracked files that are logs or case-study evidence | 10,968 of 17,113 (**64 %**): `dev/log` 5,306, `docs/case-studies` 5,662; 677 MB + 240 MB in the worktree; `.git` 400 MB; #1072: 31 GB of ladder snapshots in under six hours |
| CI gate scripts / workflows / YAML lines | 27 `scripts/check-*` / 19 / 4,814 |
| Doc-pin test files / assertions on prose | 48 (`tests/unit/docs_requirements*`) / 320 |
| Byte-equality pins on `data/meta/*invariant*.lino` | 5 sites across 12 invariant files |
| Tests / recorded durations | 4,220 `#[test]`; the 633 tests with recorded durations sum to 4,293 s (`data/meta/test-durations.lino`) |
| Traceability rows / "not yet confirmed" | 776 / **716** |
| Last three merged PRs | #1077 CI/CD (issue 1076), #1078 tool-scope grounding (issue 1075, a product fix), #1080 CI/CD (issue 1079) |

### 1.5 The frontier nobody touched

Open issues that are real prompts Formal AI could not answer: #720, #721, #722, #724 (2026-07-14), #869 (07-26), #1063 (08-25). `git log --grep` for any of them returns zero commits. The reported dialogues #800, #801, #821, #826, #827, #838, #872 and the UI complaint #447 are in the same state. `GOALS.md` names exactly these as the learning loop's frontier inputs.

## 2. Root cause

We optimise for gates and evidence we can pass instead of capability we cannot yet demonstrate. Each cycle: a gap is found, a Rust handler and a recipe describing it are added, a test pins them together, a gate protects the pin, a case study preserves the logs, a ledger records a ratchet. The vision's gap (behaviour as links) is untouched, and the next cycle has more Rust, more pins and more evidence to work around. The self-development gate then rewarded whatever satisfied it, and what satisfied it was trailers on documentation. Every step was honest; the sum is measured progress decoupled from the stated goal.

## 3. What to do differently

Ordered. D1 to D4 are one pull request for this issue. D5 to D9 are sub-issues of this issue, blocked by it, with the standing process clauses. Each item states current value, target, and test.

### D1. Make the links network the executable system of record

1. **Kernel allowlist** in `data/meta/core-boundary-ledger.lino`: `links_format.rs`, the Links Notation codec, `link_store.rs`, `substitution.rs` and `links_substitution_query/`, `event_log.rs`, `memory.rs`/`memory_sync.rs`, `SolverConfig`, the transports (`main.rs`, `server.rs`, `protocol.rs`, Telegram, `src/web/wasm-worker`), `agent.rs` sandboxing, and the new rule interpreter. Everything else is behaviour and belongs in data.
2. **Load, then query.** At startup, load `data/seed` and `data/meta` into `LinkCliLinkStore` (native) or the IndexedDB mirror (browser) and route intent matching, cue lookup, handler precedence and formalisation through link queries. `solver.rs`, `engine.rs` and `seed.rs` reference `LinkStore` because they read from it.
3. **One generic interpreter** for rule shapes 1 and 5 of `VISION.md` ("Computation Model"): `when x do y` substitutions over link CRUD, and `.lino` skills walked step by step with each step appended to the event log. Migrate the 51 pending handlers through it smallest-first by line count; delete each Rust handler when the seed rule passes the same held-out paraphrases in en, ru, hi, zh.
4. **Measured shrink ratchets, not ceilings.** Record at every release and fail the release on any non-decrease: non-kernel Rust lines (baseline: total minus kernel, computed in the PR), handler files (43), ledger pending (51), `contains("`+`starts_with("` outside the kernel (570), allowlist rows (1,309). Delete `specialized_handler_files_max` and `try_dispatch_entries_max`; a ceiling that can be raised by the same commit that exceeds it is not a ratchet.

**Test.** `scripts/check-kernel-ratchet.rs` compares the five values at `HEAD` and the previous tag. A unit test injects a seed rule for an unseen intent and asserts routing in four languages with no Rust change. Ledger pending ≤ 40 at the end of this PR.

### D2. Build the links-to-code edit path and redefine self-coding

What exists: meta-language parses Rust and JavaScript (both grammars are seed-declared) into a links network and `reconstruct_text()` returns the identical bytes (`src/coding/cst.rs:167`, `src/agentic_coding/self_ast.rs:239`; 16,074 links for `planner.rs`). What is missing: nothing edits the links and renders changed code; `structured_edit.rs` edits bytes with offsets; `substitution_compiler` emits Rust/JS/WASM only for the rule IR.

1. **Edits as link substitutions.** Express the ladder's three edit shapes as `when x do y` rules over the CST links network: member insertion into a list node, literal replacement in a string node, identifier rename across `identifier` nodes with the same binding. Pipeline: parse → links → apply rule → `reconstruct_text` → `rustfmt` → `cargo check` → `cargo test` for the touched module. Replace `structured_edit.rs` byte logic with these rules. This is the first real links → Rust and links → JavaScript path.
2. **Requirement-derived edits.** Store the self-AST census for every `src/` module (today: one) so a requirement such as "add wikiquote as a search provider" is resolved by link query (which `const` lists exist, where `WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDERS` is declared) instead of by the prompt naming the file.
3. **Definition.** "Formal AI codes itself" means: Formal AI appends or supersedes links in `data/seed`/`data/meta` that change its behaviour, or applies a link substitution to its own source, generates a held-out test, validates through the interpreter and `cargo test`, and opens the pull request. Seed edits are the first rung because they need no compiler; source edits follow through the same rule engine.

**Test.** Each of the 32 current leaves is reproduced by a committed `.lino` rule and passes `cargo check`. One requirement-shaped prompt with no file name is resolved to the right file by link query. One open "Unknown prompt" issue (#720, #721, #722, #724, #869 or #1063) is fixed end to end by `hive-mind solve --model formal-ai`: seed links appended, four-language held-out test added, pull request opened under a bot identity, CI green with no human commit on the branch.

### D3. Make the self-development metric measure the model and the behaviour

1. Attribution requires the committed evidence bundle to contain the Agent CLI stream (`agent-stream.jsonl`) whose model field is `formal-ai`, plus a `Formal-AI-Model: formal-ai <version>` trailer. A session id or evidence naming Claude, Codex, Gemini or OpenCode is rejected with the reason printed.
2. Numerator and denominator count only behaviour-changing paths: `src/`, `data/seed/`, `data/meta/` recipes and rules, `tests/`. `docs/`, `dev/`, `experiments/`, `changelog.d/` and captured artifacts are excluded on both sides.
3. Ledger rows gain `pull_request_author`; a pull request opened under a human account counts in the denominator only.
4. Recompute `v0.296.0..v0.347.0` as `metric_version 3` by appending rows. Publish the figure and its trend in `README.md`, even at 0.00 %.
5. Move the floor off `release.yml` onto its own always-visible status (dedicated workflow, README badge, weekly comment on this issue) that is red until true, with no budget, window or bypass. Releases cut on CI correctness alone. This reverses the #924 / #1066 decision; the evidence in 1.2 and #1064 is the reason.

**Test.** Replaying version 3 over the range yields no numerator path under `docs/` or `dev/` and no commit with a `-claude-` session id; a unit test feeds valid trailers with Claude-named evidence and asserts rejection.

### D4. Turn the ladder into a compile-and-test coding ladder

Keep the 32 change-shaped leaves and add, per leaf, `cargo check` (the release binary is already built in the workflow) and `cargo test --test unit <touched module>`. Composite nodes apply both children's diffs to one tree and compile it. Depth 3 and above are requirement-shaped: the prompt names the behaviour, not the file (D2.2). The root is D2's real issue. Run on pull requests, not only on dispatch; ratchet the deepest passing level; keep the 2026-08-28 failures as the baseline the ratchet starts from.

**Test.** `verify-node.sh` fails a leaf whose change does not compile; the README of each run reports per node the compile result, the test that was red then green, and the diff size; no node passes through an effect file alone.

### D5. Act on upstream benchmark zeros

1. Every failing upstream case in `external-results.lino` becomes a learning-cycle frontier input (`src/learning_cycle.rs`).
2. The external-benchmarks workflow is red when a suite's `passed` falls and yellow after three equal runs.
3. Explain in the case study why HumanEval task 0, which is seeded, scores 0 under the upstream prompt, and fix the transfer.
4. Cite the upstream row beside every curated citation (1 in `VISION.md`, 3 in `ROADMAP.md`), closing #958.

**Test.** A doc test asserts every "13/13" is within one sentence of the latest upstream row. At least one of HumanEval, MBPP or CoEdIT is above 0/20 through generalised rules with held-out paraphrases, not per-case branches.

### D6. Work the frontier queue before more CI work

Fix #720, #721, #722, #724, #869 and #1063 by generalisation with four-language held-out tests; use them as D4 leaves and D2 roots. Reproduce #447 on a phone and a desktop and fix the reported flows.

**Test.** Each closes with its paraphrase set under `data/benchmarks/` and a transcript or screenshot in its case study; none closes by a per-prompt rule.

### D7. Move evidence out of the source repository

1. Create `link-assistant/formal-ai-evidence` (or release assets) for `dev/log/`, raw case-study logs, run captures, and template snapshots. Keep here the case-study prose and a Links Notation index with `sha256`, size and URL per artifact, which is the "public knowledge as cache" pattern `VISION.md` already prescribes.
2. CI check: a pull request may add at most 2,000 non-source lines outside `docs/case-studies/issue-*/{README,requirements,solution-plan}.md`.
3. Land #1072 (git worktree instead of archive copies).

**Test.** `git ls-files dev/log docs/case-studies | wc -l` < 2,000; a fresh clone < 150 MB; every index entry resolves and its hash matches.

### D8. Collapse the gate ecosystem

1. Render the status tables in `ROADMAP.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/requirements-traceability.md` from `data/meta` ledgers; one test asserts the render is current; prose is never pinned by string. Target: `ls tests/unit | grep -c docs_` ≤ 5 (from 48).
2. Convert the 5 byte-equality pins on invariant files to clause containment (the #1065 pattern) and say so in `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
3. A new `scripts/check-*` or workflow job must retire an existing one or cite, in `data/meta/ci-gates/check-ci-gate-registry.lino`, a defect it caught in the last 30 days.
4. Record a shrink-only wall-clock ceiling for the pull-request pipeline.

**Test.** The counts above; every gate registry row has `justification`; median PR pipeline time is below the recorded ceiling.

### D9. Finish or retire the traceability column

716 of 776 rows are unconfirmed. Either fill the manual-confirmation column from the replayable session captures the agentic-CLI matrix already produces, or mark the column aspirational in its header and add no new ledger until an existing one is complete.

**Test.** Unconfirmed rows < 100, or the header carries the status and `CONTRIBUTING.md` states the rule.

## 4. What stays fixed

- Associative technology only: doublets, Links Notation, meta-language, link queries. No graphs, tables or embeddings in the runtime. This issue makes the stack more central, not less.
- Determinism, add-only history, honest metrics including 0 %, opt-in agent mode, no neural model at the steering wheel (#483 boundary).
- The no-deferral rule. D3.5 moves a gate to where bookkeeping cannot satisfy it and keeps it red until real.
- Multilingual by construction: every migrated rule ships with en, ru, hi, zh held-out paraphrases.

## 5. Document amendments

- `VISION.md`, "Current Direction": state that today the doublets store is a write-behind projection and reasoning is compiled Rust, and that D1 is the current gap. Put the upstream table beside the 13/13 sentence.
- `GOALS.md`, "Self-Evolution Goals": adopt the D2.3 definition and "measure the share of each release authored by the formal-ai model over behaviour-changing files only".
- `NON-GOALS.md`: add "Documentation, logs or ledgers about Formal AI do not count as Formal AI authoring itself"; "A gate that can be satisfied without changing behaviour is not a gate, and a ceiling that can be raised is not a ratchet"; "Vendoring run logs into the source repository is not evidence; a hashed index to an evidence store is"; "A curated benchmark number is never cited without the upstream number beside it".
- `ROADMAP.md`: a section for this issue with the D1 ratchet values at the release that closes it.

## 6. Definition of done

1. `cargo test` and the full pipeline are green on the closing pull request.
2. The five D1 ratchets and the D7/D8 counts are in the release ledger row and lower than at `v0.347.0`; the two raised ceilings no longer exist.
3. `metric_version 3` rows exist, `README.md` shows the figure, and `release.yml` no longer runs `check-self-development-release.rs` as a release condition.
4. Every current ladder leaf passes `cargo check`; at least one requirement-shaped node passes; one pull request in this repository was opened by the formal-ai model through `hive-mind solve`, changed behaviour, added a held-out test, and merged green with no human commit on the branch.
5. `external-results.lino` shows a coding suite above zero and the workflow is red on regression.

## 7. Process

- Collect data to `docs/case-studies/issue-1085/`: timeline, full requirement list (R1085-1 …), per-requirement solution plans, an existing-library survey (rule interpreters over doublets, Deep.Foundation handlers, the vendored e-graph and Datalog engines, the meta-language CST round trip), and online research on symbolic self-modification and Goodhart effects in engineering metrics.
- Verbose output wherever a root cause is not determinable from logs, in particular the metric's attribution decision, which must print why a commit did or did not count.
- File upstream issues with reproductions where the Agent CLI or Hive Mind blocks D2 (bot identity for the opened pull request, model field in session evidence).
- D1 to D4 in one pull request for this issue; D5 to D9 as sub-issues blocked by it, each with the same clauses.
- This issue is E108 and a sub-issue of #651. It absorbs or supersedes #958 (E106), #959 (E107), #954 (E102), #710 (E68), #1072.

## 8. Revision note

The first draft of this issue was re-checked premise by premise. Corrected: the current ladder is change-shaped (32 real single-file edits), not inspect-and-record; trailer-bearing commits are 125, not 186, and 72 of them are Claude sessions; 8 of the 10 most recent are docs, not all 10; pull requests are opened under konard's account by konard or hosted-model agents, not "by a human" in every case; doc-pin assertions are 320, not 405; byte-equality pins are 5 sites, not 12 files; `README.md` cites neither benchmark figure; the shrink-only ceilings were not merely static, they were raised twice; the outside-core line ceiling did fall by 0.9 %. Everything else in the first draft reproduced.
title: E108: The links network is not the system that reasons: Rust handlers, proxy self-coding metrics, and evidence weight are what block Formal AI from coding itself
